newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ posts NZ$166.8 mln surplus in 1995/96.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ posts NZ$166.8 mln surplus in 1995/96.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand on Wednesday reported it had a net consolidated surplus of NZ$166.8 million in the June year.
That compared with a $135.7 million budgeted surplus and against $129.2 million in 1994/95.
The bank said $5.3 million of the surplus was transferred to equity and the balance of $161.4 million would be paid to the government.
The bank is budgeting for a surplus of $136.7 million in the 1997 year, of which it budgets to pay $132.1 million to the government and transfer $4.6 million to equity.
The bank said the surplus is not a good indicator of management performance. It said it deals in financial markets to achieve policy goals, not to maximise its surplus.
The surplus is also dependent on the level of interest rates, and income declines as interest rates fall.
Consolidated expenditure in the year was $38.6 million, 1.9 percent under budget.
The bank is budgeting for operating expenditure of $40.4 million in 1996/97.
